title: arXiv AI papers — Tuesday, 27 October 2026 batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This inferred ordering uses dated third-party Hugging Face Daily Papers upvotes; citation evidence is limited for these recent preprints, and Semantic Scholar currently reports zero citations for each selected paper.

sections.title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
sections.abstract: StreamVibe combines an intent-aware benchmark, a streaming vision-language model, and a persistent-state harness to infer implicit user intent and adapt responses as it evolves.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a 10.7% improvement in response timing and answer quality over baselines, with a further 12.3% proactive-interaction gain from their persistent-state harness.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say real-world interactions may involve richer co-evolving user intent and environmental state than their current setting captures, and call for longer-horizon study.
sections.ranking_evidence: Hugging Face Daily Papers (27 Oct) showed 246 community upvotes at the snapshot, the highest among these five selected papers.

sections.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
sections.abstract: This paper presents a work-centric framework for digital agents organized around persistence, openness, capability families, and joint model/harness optimization.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors classify digital work along persistence and openness, define five work forms and five capability families, and frame model, harness, and joint optimization around verifiable work outcomes.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a systems perspective and synthesis, not a new controlled agent benchmark; the framework's practical value must be tested across deployed work settings.
sections.ranking_evidence: Hugging Face Daily Papers (27 Oct) showed 103 community upvotes, second-highest among these five selected papers.

sections.title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges
sections.abstract: This survey defines recursive self-improvement and organizes its trustworthiness risks around improvement validity, constraint preservation, security/privacy, and effective oversight.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide a four-stage operational framework for improvement and recursively revising the improvement mechanism, then map safeguards and evaluation needs across updates and successor systems.
sections.unique_caveat: The survey distinguishes direct RSI evidence from evidence in related systems and notes that some proposed safeguards are not yet empirically validated.
sections.ranking_evidence: Hugging Face Daily Papers (27 Oct) showed 22 community upvotes, third-highest among these five selected papers; its cross-list spans AI and security.

sections.title: S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning
sections.abstract: S3AC trains a critic to supply token-level advantages and prompt-level baselines for LLM reasoning RL, then uses difficulty-aware prompt sampling to reduce wasted rollouts.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report gains over GRPO-X across dense and mixture-of-experts models from 1.5B to 397B parameters, and sustained single-rollout training at 35B where tested critic-free baselines declined after initial gains.
sections.unique_caveat: The appendix cautions that small score differences on R1-Distill-1.5B vary across repeated evaluations; prompt scoring also adds computation, especially with larger single-rollout batches.
sections.ranking_evidence: Hugging Face Daily Papers (27 Oct) showed 16 community upvotes, fourth-highest among these five selected papers; its cross-list spans machine learning and language.

sections.title: EmbodiedLab: Benchmarking Embodied Agents That Act to Know
sections.abstract: EmbodiedLab evaluates whether an agent can use experiments in a physics-based simulated laboratory to discover unknown system properties and report knowledge grounded in its observations.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across 30 experiments in five disciplines and 14 apparatus platforms, the authors report that even the strongest tested agent succeeds less than half the time under native control, with most failures arising from apparatus interaction.
sections.unique_caveat: The evaluation is a physics-based simulation rather than physical robot deployment, and covers the benchmark's 30 experiments and 14 platforms.
sections.ranking_evidence: Hugging Face Daily Papers (27 Oct) showed 14 community upvotes, fifth among these five selected papers; it adds robotics to a shortlist otherwise concentrated on software and language agents.
